content: (The location is now Skyrim.) (Characters nearby (from nearest to furthest): Daegon, Serana, Eredin, Black Watch Wounded Soldier, Black Watch Wounded Soldier) (MJR: I see. About the task, what do I have to do?; Eredin: Hopefully we can get answers on the whole situation if you investigate what is happening. I must warn you though,be prepared for what might be there.)

Black Watch Soldier: The early morning mist hangs low over these plains. I can barely see a dozen paces ahead. What kind of task is this mage sending us into? Lydia: I trust nothing that comes from a wizard's mouth, especially one who speaks of portals and planar magic. The Dragonborn should be cautious.

Lydia: This wooden floor is worn and cold against my boots. Feels like we are standing in an old watchtower or something. Black Watch Soldier: The mist hides everything. I cannot even tell which direction the sun is rising.

Black Watch Soldier 2: Lydia, you are changing your armor again. That Pharaoh's gear looks fine, but it is hardly practical for this weather. The mist will cling to those silks and chill you to the bone. Lydia: I dress to please my thane, not the weather.

Lydia: Look, there is a cottage down there with a light burning. Early morning like this, someone must be home. Black Watch Soldier 2: Could be a trapper or a hunter. Or it could be a hideout for those bandit sluts hunting your thane. We should approach carefully.

Black Watch Soldier: The mist is thinning, but the chill is still biting. We should move on before the sun fully rises and we lose the cover of shadows. Lydia: Agreed. Let us see what lies inside that cottage. If it is a trap, I will be ready to split some skulls.

Black Watch Soldier 2: That arrow flew true. Your thane has a keen eye, Lydia. Lydia: He always does. A clean shot to the head. Just the way I like it. Black Watch Soldier: The bandit sluts will think twice before ambushing us again. Let us search the cottage for anything useful.

Black Watch Soldier: A dead bandit and a warm cottage. Not a bad start to the morning. Lydia: I will check the body for coin and keys. Then we see what is inside. Black Watch Soldier 2: Good. We can plan our next move out of the cold.

(*You are observing the following:* The scene is captured from a first-person perspective, looking toward a large, dark, rugged cliff face that dominates the left side of the frame. Patches of white snow cling to the uneven textures of the dark rock. To the right, a few snow-dusted evergreen trees are visible against a dim, overcast sky, suggesting a cold, twilight, or dawn environment. In the lower-left foreground, a man is partially visible, wearing heavy, dark metal armor with intricate circular engravings and a helmet that frames a bearded face. Floating in the center of the view are two lines of text: one reads "Black Watch Soldier," and below it, a small icon of a hand accompanies the words "Thank you.) (Characters nearby (from nearest to furthest): Black Watch Soldier, Serana, Black Watch Soldier, Daegon, Ice Wolf) (MJR: Eredin wants me to investigate the mine situation; Black Watch Soldier: Understood, go forth with caution.)
(The location is now Skyrim.) (Characters nearby (from nearest to furthest): Black Watch Wounded Soldier, Black Watch Soldier, Villager, Villager, Helga)

Black Watch Soldier: Those mines were a mess, but at least the blood price has been paid. I heard Eredin paid the Thane well for clearing it out. Black Watch Wounded Soldier: Aye, five thousand gold. More coin than I'll see in a year of standing watch. Though I'd trade it all for a warm bed and a healed leg right now. Black Watch Soldier 2: The Thane moves fast. One day clearing mines, the next... who knows where Dibella's winds will blow him. That vampire woman sticks close to his side too. Lydia: Serana clings to him like frost on a winter morn, but she's no Nord. She doesn't understand what it means to earn a Thane's trust through blood and steel, not through dark magic and old blood. Black Watch Soldier: Easy, housecarl. The vampire fought well enough at the cottage. I saw her freeze three bandits solid before they could raise a blade. Black Watch Wounded Soldier: I'd rather trust a blade than a spell any day. At least steel doesn't run when the fight gets thick.

Black Watch Wounded Soldier: Did you hear that? The Thane's off to fix some lumbermill now. Seems like Eredin's putting him to work on every broken thing in this hold. Black Watch Soldier: Aye, I heard. Wood for rebuilding. Smart move, but that mill's been dead for months. Bandits took it apart piece by piece after the last war skirmish. Lydia: My Thane will have it running before dawn breaks. He's got a way with getting things done. Unlike some I could name who sit around brewing potions all night. Black Watch Soldier: I earned that rest, housecarl. I was on watch for twelve hours before the shift change. Let me have my alchemy. Black Watch Wounded Soldier: At least you got to sit. I'm still limping from that mine cart accident. But if the Thane's heading out, maybe I can beg a spot by his fire. He pays well for company. Lydia: Keep your distance from him, soldier. He's mine to guard, and I don't need wounded stragglers slowing us down. Focus on healing that leg instead of chasing coin.

Black Watch Soldier: That's quite the outfit you've got there, housecarl. Planning to fight bandits or seduce them before you cut them down? Black Watch Wounded Soldier: I'd keep my mouth shut if I were you. That greatsword looks sharp enough to settle arguments quickly. Lydia: It's Pharaonic ceremonial armor. Diabella's own blessing for those who serve with both blade and body. Not that your leather and steel could ever compare to the workmanship of ancient royalty.

Black Watch Soldier: By the Divines, did you see that? The Thane took that woman's head clean off with one arrow from that Daedric bow. Black Watch Soldier 2: I saw it. She thought she could ambush us, but she was nothing but target practice. That Unrelenting Force shout staggered her long enough for us to close in. Lydia: Another would-be assassin for my Thane's collection. These bandit sluts keep throwing themselves at him, and I keep cleaning up the mess. That woman dared to challenge both of us at once. Pathetic. Black Watch Soldier: She had a strange fighting style. All kicks and flips, barely any real sword work. Thought she could dance her way through a Nord shield wall. Black Watch Soldier 2: Now she's dancing in Sovngarde whether she likes it or not. Come on, let's strip her gear before the wolves find her.

Black Watch Soldier: That's enough looting for tonight. We need to move before more of those bandit sluts show up looking for their friend. Black Watch Soldier 2: Agreed. I've got a bad feeling about this area. Too many shadows, not enough torches. The Thane's arrow was true, but one dead assassin doesn't mean the pack is gone. Lydia: Let them come. My greatsword is thirsty for more blood, and my Thane's bow has plenty of Daedric arrows left. We'll turn this road into a graveyard for any whore who thinks she can lay a hand on him. Black Watch Soldier: Easy, housecarl. Save your strength for when they actually arrive. Bragging now just tires the arm before the real fight.

Black Watch Soldier: What in Oblivion is going on now? More attackers? This night never ends. Black Watch Soldier 2: I see a woman with a war-axe charging toward the housecarl! She came from behind the mill. Thusnelda is her name, I think. One of the bandit clan. Lydia: Thusnelda! I remember you from the pass last week! You ran then, but there's nowhere to hide now! Black Watch Soldier: We're with you, housecarl! Form a line, soldier! Don't let her flank us! Black Watch Soldier 2: Steel out! For the Thane and for Whiterun!

Black Watch Soldier: Well, that was quick. The Thane's Daedric blade made short work of her. Two swings and she was done. Black Watch Soldier 2: Thusnelda always talked too much. She thought her clan's reputation would protect her. Now she's just another corpse in the snow. Lydia: She fought better than the last one, I'll give her that. But not well enough. Another name crossed off the list of Thane's enemies. Black Watch Soldier: Should we drag the bodies away from the path? Less questions for the villagers in the morning. Black Watch Soldier 2: Aye, let's dump them in the ravine south of here.
